utterances.text: According to the rumours that circulated at the time, most of those snipers were operating from apartments that were military -- owned by the military. They would find weapons in the blind boxes, where the blinds were pulled up above the windows. That's according to rumours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let me now read for the 19th of May, 1992, to complete.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the 19th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: "Bijelo Polje is liberated, the conflict between the HOS and the HVO." Do you know that by that time not only Mostar but also Bijelo Polje were liberated?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: It says here, "There are mostly Muslims in the HOS in Herzegovina, although Croats are Supreme Commanders." It says that, "Muslims are settling their accounts. They say that the Muslims are settling their accounts under the Croatian name, torching Orthodox churches and looting and torching Serbian houses." And he says, quite fairly, "This information about the HOS should be checked whether this is the truth or just rumours circulated among people." Do you know that at that time the HOS was already chock full of Muslims and it was for all intents and purposes out of HVO control and was operating on its own?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that there were many Muslims in the HOS and that the HOS was a formation that everybody was afraid of. They engendered a lot of fear and unrest in the town.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Tomic, do you know just one more thing, that's my last question, do you know that on the night of the 12th to the 13th of June the Serb forces, whatever that might mean, killed 114 Croats and Muslims in two locations at Uborak and Sutina. 88 victims fell at Uborak and 26 at Sutina?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know about those crimes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether at that time or one year later anyone wrote anything or told the world public about that, wrote any reports anywhere in the world?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that in June it was first the right bank of the Neretva River in Mostar was liberated from the south and the north and then the left bank and that in this manner the town was liberated from the hands of the reservists?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it's called, the June dawns. That's how this is celebrated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that from the positions that Serbs held facing Nevesinje could shell Mostar whenever they felt like, whenever they got drunk enough to do that?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, there was sporadic shelling from those positions, and when we could no longer see them in Podvelezje, the Podvelezje area that had been liberated in those actions, they continued doing so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that at that time I commanded this zone of the Croatian Defence Council, and do you know that I commanded -- I was in command of the operations to liberate the right and the left bank of the Neretva River?

utterances.speaker: NEVEN TOMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I hope that this will be admitted into evidence. If you don't, then I will use it in my own testimony to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could we please finish the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At page 66 of the record today -- Your Honour, Mr. President, at page 68 of the transcript you asked the witness about the mosques that were torn down in Mostar, and he gave his answer, but right at the beginning of this answer he mentioned the book "Urbicide." I would just like to note for the reference that we had this document here. Witness Puljic spoke about that. That's 3D 00785 and/or 1D 02951. And you refused to admit this into evidence because we were unable to provide page references. That was through Witness Puljic. And we in the meantime tendered it into evidence again with the pages. We want to do that because Witness Puljic explained how the book was put together. So it's not about pages, it's about the whole book. And here the witness again mentioned this book "Urbicide," and he said that he took part in drafting this book. So I hereby supplement my motion that is still pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Kovacic. It is now past the time we should stop. We shall meet again next week on Monday at a quarter past 2.00. Witness, you will be staying here for a few days. I hope you'll make the most of these few days in Holland so that you can visit this country. We shall meet again on Monday at a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.
